primitives.name: Player Order Statistic
primitives.verbatim_quote: Dataset / schema Same as ledger 1300: 2017–18 BigDataBall play-by-play plus NBA.com box/hustle data; 28 player statistics × five order statistics = 140 lineup predictors; players ≥50 minutes, lineups ≥25 minutes, 888 lineups, random 712/176 split.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_i': 'individual player index', 'o_{i,k}': "k-th order statistic of player i's performance metric"}
primitives.assumptions: Players' performance metrics are independently distributed; order statistics capture relative dominance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player samples fall below minimum threshold (50 min), order statistics become unreliable.

layer2.mapping: Each player’s k-th order statistic maps to a feature vector in GSE state space; ensemble classifier aggregates these into lineup efficacy score.

primitives.name: Ensemble Classifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Same as ledger 1300: seven-model unanimous classifier (tree, RF, boosting, SVM, KNN, logistic regression, LDA).
primitives.assumptions: Base learners are diverse and individually weak; majority vote ensures robustness.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If all learners agree, convergence to stable prediction; otherwise, uncertainty increases.

layer2.mapping: Ensemble kernel combines predictions from multiple learners to form a unified decision boundary in GSI belief space.

primitives.name: Lineup Efficacy Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: Test elite precision 13/15 = 86.7%; overall accuracy 52.3%; next-season restricted evaluation 20/26 = 76.9% precision vs 62.1% prevalence.
primitives.assumptions: Higher efficacy correlates with positive plus-minus per minute; score derived from classifier confidence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Scores near 0.5 indicate ambiguous or non-elite lineups; scores above 0.8 suggest strong predictive power.

layer2.mapping: Efficacy score is computed as normalized ensemble output; used in GSE to evaluate lineup transition probabilities.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight hinges on extracting latent synergy from individual player order statistics—ranked performance metrics—to infer collective lineup effectiveness. The method assumes that even without shared court time, players’ relative dominance patterns (captured via order statistics) encode sufficient information to predict elite performance. This is modeled through a 140-dimensional feature space (28 stats × 5 players), processed by a seven-model consensus classifier. The ensemble approach mitigates overfitting and enhances generalization across seasons. However, the model suffers from temporal leakage due to same-season splits, where players may reappear in different lineups. The key duality lies between individual rank-ordering and emergent team synergy—a dualism resolved via statistical aggregation rather than direct interaction modeling. Failure modes include insufficient sample size (players <50 mins) and over-reliance on static metrics without dynamic context.
